content.text:
Yes — **early Coca-Cola did contain cocaine**, in small amounts, because it used extract from **coca leaves**.

Coca-Cola was created in **1886** by pharmacist **John Pemberton**, and the original formula included coca leaf extract and kola nut extract — hence the name **Coca-Cola**. At the time, cocaine was legal and used in some medicines and tonics.

By the early **1900s**, public concern and regulation around cocaine increased. Coca-Cola began removing the active cocaine from its coca leaf ingredient, and by about **1903**, the drink no longer contained cocaine in the usual sense.

Modern Coca-Cola **does not contain cocaine**. It may still use a flavoring derived from **“spent” coca leaves**, which have had the cocaine alkaloid removed under strict regulation.
